description: Hi everyone! I am a passionate high school student and aspiring data scientist bridging the gap between theoretical astrophysics and practical computer science. For this challenge, I developed a solo-driven project for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, focusing on building an interactive, public-facing web tool that transforms complex near-infrared sky survey data into visual insights.
summary: An interactive web-based platform has been created for the purposes of conducting temporal analysis on and monitoring any transient celestial objects in real time. This tool utilizes state-of-the-art metadata tracking technologies that can detect any fluctuations in the levels of flux intensity in order to determine the presence of any variable stars and/or moving celestial bodies. By combining intricate data from space with an intuitive user interface, I have managed to solve the problem of the visualization and analysis of space data. It is critical for opening up space to all people.
details:
What It Does & How It Works My project is an interactive astronomical observation and temporal analysis platform designed to track celestial transient sources in real time. Users can monitor specific target objects (such as high-latitude transient sources) via a live metadata dashboard that displays celestial coordinates, tracking status, and flux intensity variances across survey intervals. By analyzing positional shifts and fluctuations in infrared and light brightness, the platform helps identify potential variable stellar activity and moving cosmic bodies.

Benefits & Intended Impact Raw astronomical and space survey datasets are often difficult for students, citizen scientists, and general enthusiasts to navigate. My platform bridges that gap by transforming complex space telemetry and flux data into a clean, readable visual interface. The intended impact is to democratize space exploration, allowing anyone with a web browser to explore dynamic cosmic phenomena and understand how astronomers detect active celestial objects.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend Technologies: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript
  • Data Visualization & Rendering: HTML5 Canvas and interactive UI components for plotting temporal flux intensity and object metadata
  • Data Integration: Real-time astronomical APIs and structured JSON survey datasets
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio Code with Live Server for testing and deployment

Creativity & Design Considerations Instead of presenting users with raw tables of numbers, I designed a mission-control-style dark-mode interface featuring color-coded status indicators, dynamic observation notes, and intuitive coordinate readouts. Key factors considered during development include data accuracy, responsive layout design across different screen sizes, and ensuring high visual contrast so users can easily spot anomalies and flux variances without visual fatigue.
